brief: cloudCover() was added at iteration 3 and has exactly one reader: the rain roll. Its own probe measured a median 27 s — half a day — between cover crossing 0.5 and the first drop, and the town uses none of it. Everything that reacts to weather reads `raining` instead, a boolean that flips in one frame: the washing lines are gated `!raining` at ~line 2401 and so vanish between two frames, and umbrellas go up at line 1297 only once the rain has already started. Give the town a state for 'weather is coming', read off cover, so that a viewer watching the wide shot sees the lane prepare before the sky opens. Pick two or three readers with the strongest read rather than wiring all of them — the washing coming in is the most legible single thing in the frame — and make each one a transition, not a pop.
successLooksLike: On a building front you can watch the town get ready before the first drop lands, and the filmstrip shows no frame where the washing disappears all at once.
avoid: Do not add a second predicate for 'about to rain' — one function, many readers (see the one-predicate law). Do not touch stepClouds' rate cap or the cover>0.66 rain gate: iteration 3 proved both with a probe that still depends on them.
